properties.crop: dairy pasture and small farmsteads
properties.note: John Hunter's dairy and vegetable farm near Fitch and Oakdale (early 1850s); Silver Terrace 'garden lots' for small farms (1859); homestead tracts of the 1860s; the 1869 Coast Survey map shows 'a handful of scattered farmsteads'; the 1899-1900 Sanborn maps label much of the Bay View, Bay Park, Paul and Garden tracts 'cultivated by market gardeners or in use as pasture for local dairies' (Bayview-Hunters Point context statement, Kelley & VerPlanck 2010). Outline ESTIMATED: level land between San Bruno Ave, the Islais marsh, Oakdale Ave, South Basin and Bayview Hill, on valley-floor units or ground under 7 degrees. Share ESTIMATED.

properties.crop: market gardens (Chinese, then Italian, Portuguese and Maltese growers), greenhouses
properties.note: 'By the last quarter of the nineteenth century, much of the level land of the Bayview had come under cultivation by truck farmers' (theme period 1880-1974); Chronicle 17 Nov 1889: Italian market gardens 'along the San Bruno Road, in the San Miguel Ranch, along the borders of the Presidio Reservation, and in South San Francisco'; the Hudson Tract was vegetable gardens on the 1914 Sanborn maps; row houses took the farms east of 3rd St in the 1920s, 'a handful of truck farms remained in business until the 2000s' (Bayview-Hunters Point context statement). year_end ESTIMATED (most gone by 1950).

properties.crop: truck gardens and hay fields around Washerwoman's Lagoon (cultivated ground, 1857 survey)
properties.note: Outline = the cultivated-ground symbol (ladders of short dashes) of the US Coast Survey sheet 'City of San Francisco and its vicinity' (A.F. Rodgers plane-table survey, 1:10,000, published 1857; Rumsey 6811.000), detected by texture and georeferenced on the sheet's graticule and today's street grid (about +-20 m in the city, more at the sheet edge); parcels merged, roads and houses between them included. properties.crop: dairy pasture (about 30 dairies between Van Ness Ave and the Presidio)
properties.note: Hatman's dairy ranch on the block Union / Filbert / Franklin / Gough 1861, 'one of the first'; by the early 1870s at least 30 dairies of 60-200 cows between Van Ness Ave and the Presidio; the Board of Health moved the dairies out in the 1880s (Chronicle 1947 on FoundSF; year_end ESTIMATED from 'the 80s'). Outline ESTIMATED: Van Ness - Lyon, Pacific Ave to the sand north of Lombard ('to the north were sand dunes stretching to Black Point'), on ground under 12 degrees, without the lagoon and the dune sand.

properties.crop: dairy pasture ('milch ranches', Swiss dairymen)
properties.note: George Ulshofer's milch ranch from 1859 or 1860, the first streets mapped on it in 1872 (Wikipedia, Glen Park, after the Glen Park Neighborhoods History Project); 'farms sprang up - dairy farms, duck farms, pig farms'; the electric railway of 1892 and the refugees of 1906 brought the houses (FoundSF, Glen Park: SF's 'Little Switzerland'). Four dairies on an 1861 survey and dairies moving here from Cow Hollow are reported by the History Project but were seen only as a search summary (UNVERIFIED). Outline ESTIMATED: the creek valley (Chenery / Bosworth St) and the Sunnyside valley along Monterey Blvd on ground under 12 degrees, outside Dondero's truck gardens. Share and dates ESTIMATED.

properties.crop: truck gardens of the upper Islais Creek valley (the Genoese growers' 'cagnada rica')
properties.note: Outline traced from R.S. Dondero, 'The Italian Settlement of San Francisco' (MA thesis, UC Berkeley, 1953), p.57: map of the large farming and dairy areas of 1900, as reproduced in the OMI historic context statement (Brandi & LaBounty 2010, p.10; 374 x 227 px, fitted to Sloat Blvd, 19th Ave, Sunset Blvd, Junipero Serra Blvd, Ocean Ave, Alemany Blvd and Mission St, about +-50 m); a schematic thesis map, cut here only where the ground is water, marsh, mobile dune or steeper than 15 degrees. The belt along Islais Creek (Cayuga Ave, Alemany Blvd) from the county line to the Bernal Cut, with a lobe up the creek to Glen Park. Italian, German, Swiss and Irish farmers and dairymen from the 1860s; a Chinese cabbage farm stood where Balboa High School is (Ingleside Light, 'A brief history of the Excelsior and Outer Mission districts'); farms survived 'in or around Ocean View and San Jose Avenue until the 1940s' (Dondero, via the OMI context statement). Start years ESTIMATED.

properties.crop: barley, potatoes, hay and cattle (Ocean House Road ranches)
properties.note: The 1880 census lists 11 farmers and dairymen on the Ocean House Road (Lagomarsino, Burfriend, DeHaro, Riley ...); the sandy soil was called ideal for vegetables as early as 1855 (Hutchings' California Magazine, via the OMI context statement); the Greene family grew barley and potatoes and ran cattle between Stern Grove and Lake Merced from the 1850s (Parkside context statement; their ranch north of Sloat Blvd is not drawn). Share and dates ESTIMATED; outline = Dondero's 1900 area (next row).

properties.crop: truck gardens: potatoes, cabbages, artichokes (Italian tenants of the Spring Valley Water Co.)
properties.note: Outline traced from R.S. Dondero, 'The Italian Settlement of San Francisco' (MA thesis, UC Berkeley, 1953), p.57: map of the large farming and dairy areas of 1900, as reproduced in the OMI historic context statement (Brandi & LaBounty 2010, p.10; 374 x 227 px, fitted to Sloat Blvd, 19th Ave, Sunset Blvd, Junipero Serra Blvd, Ocean Ave, Alemany Blvd and Mission St, about +-50 m); a schematic thesis map, cut here only where the ground is water, marsh, mobile dune or steeper than 15 degrees. 'By 1900, Italian-operated farms stretched from today's Villas Parkmerced, east to Urbano Drive, north to Sloat Blvd and west to Sunset Blvd'; Spring Valley leased out about 350 acres near Lake Merced from the late 1880s (Parkside context statement, after Dondero and Kortum); 'from where West Portal is today to State College was vegetable farms run by the Lagomarsino family' (c.1910, in Brandi 2003). A 1928 aerial shows the land south of Sloat Blvd still 'leased and under cultivation' (Parkside context statement p.16); house tracts, Stonestown and the State College campus took it between the 1920s and the 1950s (the buildings date each cell). year_end ESTIMATED.

properties.crop: barley, potatoes and hay (ranches of the 1850s-60s)
properties.note: Same history as the Colma district across the county line (pen_colma: grain 1858-65, truck gardens 1870-80, 80 %); dates taken from it so the two sides agree. LOW. The 1869 Coast Survey map (surveyed 1867-68) shows fenced lots and farmhouses east of the lake down to the county line. Spring Valley bought the land round the lake from 1877 (2,000 acres from the county line to Sloat Blvd, Junipero Serra to the ocean) and leased about 350 acres of it to vegetable growers (Parkside context statement). Outline ESTIMATED: valley-floor units of USGS OF 2006-1037 between the lake's east shore, Junipero Serra Blvd and the county line, outside Dondero's 1900 area.

properties.crop: truck gardens (tenants of the Spring Valley Water Co.)
properties.note: Same history as the Colma district across the county line (pen_colma: grain 1858-65, truck gardens 1870-80, 80 %); dates taken from it so the two sides agree. LOW. 'Spring Valley ejects tenants: water company claims vegetable gardens pollute city's supply' (Chronicle 17 Aug 1904, via the OMI context statement) - how much of this ground the tenants worked is not mapped; the San Francisco Golf Club took the south-east shore in 1915 (data/tables/golf_courses.csv; year_end), Parkmerced the rest after 1940. Outline ESTIMATED as in the grain row.

properties.crop: market gardens, potatoes, hay and grain, nurseries and orchards (cultivated ground, 1857 survey)
properties.note: Outline = the cultivated-ground symbol (ladders of short dashes) of the US Coast Survey sheet 'City of San Francisco and its vicinity' (A.F. Rodgers plane-table survey, 1:10,000, published 1857; Rumsey 6811.000), detected by texture and georeferenced on the sheet's graticule and today's street grid (about +-20 m in the city, more at the sheet edge); parcels merged, roads and houses between them included. The Mission plank road (1851) and Folsom plank road (1852) turned the Mission valley from cattle range to truck farming (Market & Octavia context statement); John Center, who came in 1849, began by raising vegetables on rented land near the Mission; the 1857 sheet shows truck farms watered by windmill pumps (Showplace Square context statement); 'the Mission valley floor became a crazy quilt of rural homesteads, farms, produce gardens and estates ... farms and gardens filled the valley right up to the borders of the lagoons' (City within a City, Mission District context statement). Fields west of Castro St lie in Horner's Addition / Rancho San Miguel. Built over 1860s-1880s (the buildings and extent snapshots date each cell); year_end = estimated end of the last gardens. Start years ESTIMATED.

The Mission plank road (1851) and Folsom plank road (1852) turned the Mission valley from cattle range to truck farming (Market & Octavia context statement); John Center, who came in 1849, began by raising vegetables on rented land near the Mission; the 1857 sheet shows truck farms watered by windmill pumps (Showplace Square context statement); 'the Mission valley floor became a crazy quilt of rural homesteads, farms, produce gardens and estates ... farms and gardens filled the valley right up to the borders of the lagoons' (City within a City, Mission District context statement). Fields west of Castro St lie in Horner's Addition / Rancho San Miguel. Built over 1860s-1880s (the buildings and extent snapshots date each cell); year_end = estimated end of the last gardens. Start years ESTIMATED.

properties.crop: truck gardens (Italian, Irish and German growers)
properties.note: Outline traced from R.S. Dondero, 'The Italian Settlement of San Francisco' (MA thesis, UC Berkeley, 1953), p.57: map of the large farming and dairy areas of 1900, as reproduced in the OMI historic context statement (Brandi & LaBounty 2010, p.10; 374 x 227 px, fitted to Sloat Blvd, 19th Ave, Sunset Blvd, Junipero Serra Blvd, Ocean Ave, Alemany Blvd and Mission St, about +-50 m); a schematic thesis map, cut here only where the ground is water, marsh, mobile dune or steeper than 15 degrees. Ocean View was platted in the 1860s but stayed farmland; 17 farmers and dairymen in the 1880 census; 'the valleys on the southern and eastern inclines of Merced Heights were cultivated and farmed into the mid-20th century'; some farms lasted until the 1940s (OMI context statement). Start years ESTIMATED.

properties.crop: truck gardens (Italian, Irish and German growers)
properties.note: Same history as the Colma district across the county line (pen_colma: grain 1858-65, truck gardens 1870-80, 80 %); dates taken from it so the two sides agree. properties.crop: truck gardens
properties.note: Same history as the Colma district across the county line (pen_colma: grain 1858-65, truck gardens 1870-80, 80 %); dates taken from it so the two sides agree. 'As late as 1910 1,200 Italian giardinieri (truck farmers) worked some 8,000 acres on San Francisco's south side' (Ingleside Light, 'A brief history of the Excelsior and Outer Mission districts'). Built up after 1906 and through the 1920s (the buildings date each cell); year_end ESTIMATED. Outline ESTIMATED as in the grain row.

properties.crop: dairy farms and cattle corrals (stock held for Butchertown)
properties.note: University Mound Survey 1862-63: about 400 acres bounded by Oxford St, San Bruno Ave, Silver Ave and Olmstead St. 'In the 1870s and 1880s the district was largely characterized by cattle-related uses': corrals for the Butchertown drives, Perini's dairy (1867), Kelly's (1873), 11 milk dealers by 1880; 'no dairy uses in the area after 1921' (770 Woolsey St landmark designation report, 2019). Outline = the survey's bounds on ground under 12 degrees; share ESTIMATED.

properties.crop: produce farms and truck gardens
properties.note: 'Small-scale produce farms, dairies and cut-flower nurseries' (770 Woolsey report); in the early 1900s the Portola 'remained largely agricultural', with greenhouses west of Charter Oak Ave and truck gardens east of it to the bay (FoundSF, The Portola District); Siri's large vegetable gardens went to McLaren Park in the 1930s-50s. Share and dates ESTIMATED.

properties.crop: cut-flower nurseries and greenhouses (the Garden District)
properties.note: First nursery 1865 (Golden Acre, San Bruno Ave); three more in 1880; 16 by 1900; peak in 1925 with 21 nurseries 'covering upwards of thirty blocks' (of about 100: share 0.3); ten left by 1940, five in 1970; the last, the University Mound Nursery at 770 Woolsey St, closed in 1990 (landmark designation report, 2019, table 1). Which blocks is not mapped here (share on the survey's ground, ESTIMATED): the 1914 Sanborn sheets and the 1938 aerial photographs show every greenhouse.

properties.crop: market gardens (Italian and Chinese growers)
properties.note: Chronicle 17 Nov 1889: Italian market gardens 'along the borders of the Presidio Reservation' (quoted in the Bayview-Hunters Point context statement, p.61); Presidio Terrace (1898) was laid out 'on former vegetable gardens' (Wiley 2000, via Brandi 2003 note 51). LOW: the strip south of the Presidio wall from Lyon St to 6th Ave down to California St is a generalisation of these two sentences; share and dates ESTIMATED.

properties.crop: hay, grain and dairy ranches
properties.note: Same history as the Colma district across the county line (pen_colma: grain 1858-65, truck gardens 1870-80, 80 %); dates taken from it so the two sides agree. Outline ESTIMATED: the valley floor and lower slopes (valley-floor units or ground under 7 degrees) between the McLaren ridge (Mansell St), the bay marsh at Bayshore Blvd and the county line.

properties.crop: truck gardens irrigated by windmills (Italian and Maltese growers), nurseries
properties.note: Same history as the Colma district across the county line (pen_colma: grain 1858-65, truck gardens 1870-80, 80 %); dates taken from it so the two sides agree. 'Valley of the Windmills', after the pumps that watered the fields (Wikipedia, citing LaBounty, SF Heritage 2021); a Colombo Market family farmed vegetables here 1883-1929 (Brandi 2003, note 43). Ended by the house rows of the 1920s-40s and the Sunnydale project (first tenants March 1941, data/tables/known_building_dates.csv): year_end ESTIMATED. Outline ESTIMATED as in the grain row.

properties.crop: potatoes and vegetables (Arata, Bottini, DeMartini and Lagomarsino farms on Sutro's Rancho San Miguel)
properties.note: Sutro leased the level ground of Rancho San Miguel (about 200 acres) to Italian farmers: 'most of Sutro's land bounded by today's Portola, Kensington, Taraval and Wawona streets'; 'the sandy soil was ideal for vegetables, particularly potatoes'; Burfiend's potato ranch opposite the Alms House from 1860, farmers half a mile from it by 1870, Lagomarsinos on the land by 1887; the estate could be sold from 1909 (St. Francis Wood 1912, Forest Hill 1913, Twin Peaks tunnel 1918) (Brandi 2003). Outline = those four streets, on ground under 12 degrees incl. the stabilised sand; start years and year_end ESTIMATED.

properties.crop: truck gardens and a dairy
properties.note: Outline traced from R.S. Dondero, 'The Italian Settlement of San Francisco' (MA thesis, UC Berkeley, 1953), p.57: map of the large farming and dairy areas of 1900, as reproduced in the OMI historic context statement (Brandi & LaBounty 2010, p.10; 374 x 227 px, fitted to Sloat Blvd, 19th Ave, Sunset Blvd, Junipero Serra Blvd, Ocean Ave, Alemany Blvd and Mission St, about +-50 m); a schematic thesis map, cut here only where the ground is water, marsh, mobile dune or steeper than 15 degrees. North of Ocean Ave around today's Westwood Park and the Balboa Reservoir; the east half of the House of Refuge lot beside it 'has always raised large crops' (Chronicle 24 Nov 1872, via the OMI context statement). Westwood Park was built in the 1920s (Brandi 2003). Start years and year_end ESTIMATED.
